notes: Recall/precision checklist for evaluating extraction quality, not an exact-match target -- a correct extraction phrases each requirement differently from source.quote below.
source.spans marks the offsets a requirement originates from in the given document_path; source.quote is those spans' text, joined with ' ... ' when there is more than one span.

Two source files: the main RFQ (.docx) and Attachment B (.docx, the salient-characteristics list for the AquaSept High Speed Kit) -- document_path differs by topic depending on which file the citation is from. Attachment A (.xlsx, the pricing/compliance schedule) is referenced by the RFQ text but contributes no citations of its own: its columns are filled in by the bidder, the instruction to do so lives in the RFQ.

No excluded_clauses list: text that is not a bidder requirement at all (SDVOSB set-aside eligibility criteria cited by clause number only, with no elaborated body text in this document; FAR 52.212-2 evaluation-factor language; delivery/performance-period terms with no instruction to represent them in the quote) is simply absent here.

The RFQ's own item (f) says to put Country of Origin "see column A", but Attachment A's actual Country of Origin column is J, not A -- a real inconsistency in the source document, left as-is rather than silently corrected.

authorized_distributor_letter (item d) and gray_market_verification (item g) are two separate topics, not merged: each has independent pass/fail meaning (a bidder could provide the letter without addressing gray-market status, or vice versa), even though both trace back to the same underlying sourcing fact in this application.

salient_characteristics_compliance was split into 9 topics, one per Attachment B bullet: each has independent pass/fail meaning (a product can meet 8 of 9 characteristics), unlike a single indivisible form -- see buy_american_certificate below for the opposite case.

buy_american_certificate uses two spans: item (e)'s 'Product must comply with the Buy American Act...' (the substantive obligation) plus the FAR 52.225-2 certificate provision (the procedural mechanism for disclosing it). Anchoring only to the certificate provision would make honest disclosure of a non-qualifying country of origin read as compliant just because the paperwork was filled out correctly -- the RFQ never labels a foreign/non-TAA offer 'non-responsive' outright, but item (e) does say the product itself 'must comply', which is the textual basis for treating an honestly-disclosed non-qualifying origin as non_compliant rather than compliant. Unlike salient_characteristics_compliance, buy_american_certificate's (a)(1)-(3) sub-clauses stay merged as one topic: they are one certificate filled out as a whole, with no independent pass/fail meaning per sub-clause.

requirements.description: Product must comply with the Buy American Act and Trade Agreements Act, and the quote must certify -- per the Buy American Certificate (FAR 52.225-2) -- whether each end product is a domestic or foreign end product, and whether foreign end products exceed 55% domestic content.

source.quote:
Product must comply with the Buy American Act; Trade Agreement Act and all other clauses found in the FAR and any agency-specific regulations that are relevant and specific to this solicitation ... (a)(1) The Offeror certifies that each end product, except those listed in paragraph (b) of this provision, is a domestic end product and that each domestic end product listed in paragraph (c) of this provision contains a critical component.
(2) The Offeror shall list as foreign end products those end products manufactured in the United States that do not qualify as domestic end products. For those foreign end products that do not consist wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both, the Offeror shall also indicate whether these foreign end products exceed 55 percent domestic content, except for those that are COTS items. If the percentage of the domestic content is unknown, select “no”.
(3) The Offeror shall separately list the line item numbers of domestic end products that contain a critical component (see FAR 25.105).
